title: Let Deepest Silence All Around
description: Let Deepest Silence All Around in Tonic Solfa to CAITHNESS, doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 6 verses and a piano.
about: Joseph John Gurney wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 464 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Silent Worship”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to CAITHNESS; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Let deep-est si-lence all a-round Its peace-ful shel-ter spread; So shall the liv-ing word a-bound, The word that wakes the dead.

lines: Let deepest silence all around
Its peaceful shelter spread;
So shall the living word abound,
The word that wakes the dead.
How sweet to wait upon the Lord
In stillness and in prayer!
What though no preacher speak the word
A minister is there:
He knows to bend the heart of steel,
He bows the loftiest soul;
O'er all we think and all we feel,
How matchless his control!
And, O, how precious is his love
In tender mercy given;
It whispers of the blest above,
And stays the soul on heaven.
From mind to mind, in streams of joy,
The holy influence spreads;
'T is peace, 'tis praise without alloy,
For God that influence sheds.
To thee, O God, we still will pray,
And praise thee as before;
For this thy glorious gospel-day,
Teach us to praise thee more.

licence: Public domain: Joseph John Gurney died in 1847.
credits: Words by Joseph John Gurney (1788–1847), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to CAITHNESS by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
